_comment: Godot feature build profile for the custom web export template. Read by
SCons (`build_profile=` in scripts/build-web-template.sh), which takes
`disabled_classes` and `disabled_build_options` and ignores every other
key — which is what lets `_why` live here rather than in a file that can
drift from it.
`_why` is not decoration. Every entry in `disabled_build_options` must
have one, and tests/unit/test_web_build_profile.gd fails if it does not:
a line removed from the engine without a stated reason is the failure
mode this whole file exists to avoid. That test also scans src/ for the
classes each disabled module provides, so turning something off that the
game actually uses goes red in `make gut` rather than in a browser.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY STILL ON, because a scan of src/ says the game needs
it and the issue that asked for this file guessed otherwise:
csg   — the whole 3D bay is built from CSGCombiner3D/CSGBox3D/
CSGCylinder3D/CSGPolygon3D at runtime (src/world/garage.gd,
car.gd, grime.gd, wash_jet.gd, mesh_car.gd). Cutting it was on
the candidate list and would have shipped an empty garage.
svg   — no class names it, so the scan cannot defend it. The default
theme rasterises its icons through ImageLoaderSVG at runtime,
and the settings screen's CheckButton is drawn from two of
them; without the module the toggle renders blank.
noise — FastNoiseLite, in src/world/.
webp  — no class names it either. #217 imports the model textures
lossy, and a lossy .ctex is a WebP inside a container.
bcdec — the bundle ships S3TC/BPTC textures (the Web preset's
vram_texture_compression/for_desktop=true). Where a browser
exposes neither, this is what decodes them in software instead
of dropping the texture.
godot_physics_3d — src/world/ raycasts against StaticBody3D through
PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D. This is the one "DEFAULT"
resolves to; jolt_physics is the one that goes, and the
entry for it below has the reading that settles which.
NOT DISABLED THOUGH IT COULD BE: `deprecated=no` strips the engine's
compatibility shims. It is worth a few hundred KB and it is not here,
because a GDScript call into a removed shim fails at the moment that line
runs — in a browser, on a path a smoke test may never take — and nothing
in CI would catch it. Two of the levers the issue asked for are absent
for the opposite reason: `optimize=size` is already the web platform's
default (platform/web/detect.py's get_flags(), with its own comment about
-Os beating -O3 by ~5 MB), and `production=yes` is what the official
templates are built with. Neither buys a byte over stock. Everything
measured in the pull request that added this file came from the list
below.

_why.disable_navigation_2d: No navmesh anywhere in the game; the bay is a fixed set and nothing pathfinds.
_why.disable_navigation_3d: Same. Drops the 3D navigation server as well as the module below.
_why.disable_physics_2d: The game is 3D plus Control-node UI. Godot builds a 2D physics server regardless of whether a scene has a 2D node in it; this is the option that stops it.
_why.disable_xr: No headset story, now or planned. Covers the XR server and nodes; the three XR modules below are the drivers that would have plugged into it.
_why.minizip: Packs are loaded as .pck, which is Godot's own format and not a zip. minizip is what reads a .zip resource pack — a thing this game never does.
_why.module_astcenc_enabled: ASTC compressor. The Web preset sets vram_texture_compression/for_mobile=false, so nothing in the bundle is ASTC, and compression happens in the editor regardless.
_why.module_basis_universal_enabled: No texture is imported as Basis Universal; the import pass produces S3TC/BPTC .ctex.
_why.module_betsy_enabled: GPU texture compressor, used by the editor's import pass. A template never compresses a texture.
_why.module_bmp_enabled: Runtime .bmp loader. Every image in assets/ is .png or .jpg, and all of them are imported to .ctex before they reach the pack.
_why.module_camera_enabled: CameraServer/CameraFeed — the webcam, not Camera3D. Camera3D lives in scene/3d and is unaffected.
_why.module_cvtt_enabled: CPU BC compressor, editor-side like betsy.
_why.module_enet_enabled: ENet transport. The game has no network layer at all.
_why.module_fbx_enabled: Runtime .fbx import. src-models/ exports .glb, and both formats are baked to scenes by the editor long before a template sees them.
_why.module_gltf_enabled: Runtime .glb/.gltf import. The fifteen .glb files under assets/ are imported once by the editor and travel in the pack as scenes and meshes — verified by exporting and reading the pack, which contains no glTF document.
_why.module_godot_physics_2d_enabled: The 2D server implementation behind disable_physics_2d above.
_why.module_gridmap_enabled: No GridMap or MeshLibrary in any scene.
_why.module_hdr_enabled: Runtime Radiance .hdr loader. The sky is procedural; there is no HDR panorama.
_why.module_interactive_music_enabled: AudioStreamInteractive/Playlist/Synchronized. The title theme is arithmetic (src/core/fanfare.gd), not a stem-based track.
_why.module_jolt_physics_enabled: The second of the two 3D physics engines, and the one that is not running. Both register themselves with PhysicsServer3DManager, but only modules/godot_physics_3d/register_types.cpp calls set_default_server("GodotPhysics3D") — Jolt registers and stops — and project.godot leaves physics/3d/physics_engine at "DEFAULT", which is exactly what that call decides. So this is a whole physics engine compiled into the bundle for nobody: 1,369,337 B raw and 413,388 B gzip, measured by building the template both ways and diffing godot.wasm. Turning it back on means naming it in project.godot too, and re-testing the game against a different solver.
_why.module_jpg_enabled: Runtime .jpg loader. The two .jpg files in assets/ are imported to .ctex like every other texture.
_why.module_jsonrpc_enabled: JSONRPC exists for the editor's language-server protocol. Nothing in a shipped game speaks it.
_why.module_lightmapper_rd_enabled: The lightmap baker, which is an editor tool and needs a RenderingDevice the Compatibility renderer does not have. Baked lightmaps would still render; there are none.
_why.module_mbedtls_enabled: TLS and the Crypto/X509/HMAC classes. The game makes no network request, and the high-score table is local (user:// through IndexedDB).
_why.module_meshoptimizer_enabled: Mesh simplification for LOD generation, which happens during import. The LODs it produced are already inside the imported meshes.
_why.module_mobile_vr_enabled: MobileVRInterface — an XR driver, see disable_xr.
_why.module_mp3_enabled: Every sound in the game is synthesized into an AudioStreamWAV at startup (src/core/bell.gd, tool_noise.gd, timbre.gd). There is not one audio file in the repository.
_why.module_msdfgen_enabled: MSDF font atlas generation, an import-time step. Neither of the two faces is imported with MSDF on.
_why.module_multiplayer_enabled: SceneMultiplayer and the replication nodes. Single-player, offline.
_why.module_objectdb_profiler_enabled: A debugger-side profiler. A release template has no debugger attached.
_why.module_ogg_enabled: Ogg container support, only ever reached through the vorbis module below.
_why.module_openxr_enabled: An XR driver, see disable_xr. Also the largest of the three.
_why.module_raycast_enabled: Embree, used by the lightmap baker. Already off for web upstream (platform/web/detect.py's get_flags()); listed so the profile states the full set rather than inheriting part of it silently.
_why.module_regex_enabled: RegEx/RegExMatch, and the ~1 MB of PCRE2 behind them. No script under src/ uses either — the one RegEx in the repository is in tests/unit/test_patch_flash.gd, which never reaches the pack. This is the entry most likely to bite someone later, which is exactly what test_web_build_profile.gd's scan is for.
_why.module_text_server_adv_enabled: The advanced text server and its embedded ICU tables — bidirectional text, complex-script shaping, and the largest single line item in this file. The entry below is what replaces it. Localising into a script that needs shaping means turning this back on.
_why.module_text_server_fb_enabled: The only `true` in this object, and it is not optional. modules/text_server_fb/config.py's is_enabled() returns False — 'The module is disabled by default. Use module_text_server_fb_enabled=yes to enable it.' — so turning the advanced server off without turning this on leaves a build with no text server at all. It does not fail to compile and it does not fail to export: it boots, renders the 3D bay correctly, and draws every label as nothing. That is what the first build of this profile did, and a screenshot of the title screen is what found it, which is why scripts/build-web-template.sh now reads modules/modules_enabled.gen.h afterwards and requires this module by name. What the fallback server gives up is complex-script shaping and bidirectional text; what the game asks of it is Latin, left to right, in two pixel faces.
_why.module_theora_enabled: Video playback. There is no video.
_why.module_upnp_enabled: Port forwarding for a network layer that does not exist.
_why.module_vhacd_enabled: Convex decomposition. Reachable at runtime through MeshInstance3D.create_multiple_convex_collisions(); the two colliders the game makes are hand-authored CollisionShape3Ds (src/world/car.gd, mesh_car.gd).
_why.module_visual_shader_enabled: VisualShader and its node graph. Both of the game's shaders are hand-written .gdshader text (src/world/).
_why.module_vorbis_enabled: See module_mp3_enabled — no audio files, only synthesis.
_why.module_xatlas_unwrap_enabled: Lightmap UV unwrapping, an editor operation on an ArrayMesh.
_why.module_zip_enabled: ZIPReader/ZIPPacker, the scripting side of minizip above.
